schema.source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
schema.description: {{COMPANY_NAME}} reusable Merlino Catalogue threat-profile template for System Integrator / MSP organisations. TP-04 models Privileged Access Compromise across privileged human and workload identities: targeting, credential/session/token acquisition, privilege discovery, cloud/domain/local valid-account abuse, PIM/JIT activation, role/group escalation, password-vault and cloud-secret access, persistence through accounts/credentials/devices/applications, privileged remote administration and selected defense impairment. Cloud techniques are core; Active Directory, endpoint, RMM and customer-specific techniques are explicitly marked conditional. The organisation is represented by {{COMPANY_NAME}} for rapid reuse. Records are Pick=true because every row is intentionally included in the candidate TP-04 profile.

data.Name: TP-04 | Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Obtain exposed, leaked or previously stolen credentials associated with administrators, engineers, service accounts or personnel who hold elevated access. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Privileged credentials are disproportionately valuable in system-integrator/MSP environments because a single identity may control internal cloud services, customer environments, support systems, secrets or administrative tooling. Applicability: Core. Primary privileged assets at risk: Privileged user accounts, Cloud administrators, Service accounts, Support administrators, Customer administration identities. Attack-path stage: Target Privileged Identity. Detection opportunities: Credential exposure monitoring; Entra ID Protection leaked-credential detections; Correlate exposed identities with privileged-role inventory. Defensive considerations: Dedicated privileged identities; Phishing-resistant MFA; No credential reuse; Monitor credential exposure.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-04 | Generic System Integrator / MSP privileged-access profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Privileged credentials are disproportionately valuable in system-integrator/MSP environments because a single identity may control internal cloud services, customer environments, support systems, secrets or administrative tooling. Applicability=Core; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-04 models targeting, acquisition, discovery, use, escalation and persistence of high-privilege identities and authentication material. It covers cloud administrators, customer administrative accounts, service accounts, application identities, PAM/PIM-eligible identities and—where applicable—Active Directory, local administrator, RMM and administrative-workstation credentials. TP-04 is intentionally identity/privilege-centric: detailed customer pivot belongs to TP-03, software supply-chain compromise to TP-05, and ransomware/destructive impact to TP-06. Conditional records must be filtered against the actual technology and customer-access model. This entry is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behavior has occurred.

data.Name: TP-04 | Gather Victim Identity Information: Email Addresses
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Collect corporate email addresses that can be correlated with technical or administrative responsibilities. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Administrative identities may be discoverable through company websites, events, partner directories, public repositories and social media. This supports targeted phishing, password spraying and impersonation. Applicability: Core. Primary privileged assets at risk: Cloud administrators, Developers, Support engineers, Security personnel. Attack-path stage: Target Privileged Identity. Detection opportunities: Password-spray correlation against privileged users; Threat-intelligence monitoring for targeted identities. Defensive considerations: Separate administrative UPNs where appropriate; Reduce public exposure of privileged account identifiers.

data.Name: TP-04 | Gather Victim Identity Information: Employee Names
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Identify employees likely to hold elevated privileges, operate managed services or administer sensitive systems. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Knowing who manages identity, Azure, M365, networking, CI/CD or customers allows an adversary to focus social engineering on accounts with the greatest blast radius. Applicability: Core. Primary privileged assets at risk: Administrators, Cloud engineers, Help desk, Security team, Customer support personnel. Attack-path stage: Target Privileged Identity. Detection opportunities: User-reported targeted social engineering; Brand and impersonation monitoring. Defensive considerations: Role separation; Minimise public disclosure of privileged responsibility.

data.Name: TP-04 | Gather Victim Org Information: Identify Roles
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Map organisational roles to identify users likely to possess Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator, Azure Owner, subscription administrator, domain administrator, service-account management or customer support privileges. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: System integrators often have concentrated administrative expertise. Role discovery enables precise targeting of the identities that can change authentication, roles, secrets or customer access. Applicability: Core. Primary privileged assets at risk: Entra privileged roles, Azure RBAC, AD administrative groups, Support administrators, Service owners. Attack-path stage: Target Privileged Identity. Detection opportunities: Monitor targeted phishing against privileged-role holders; Identity attack-surface review. Defensive considerations: Maintain privileged-role inventory; Separate privileged accounts from public personas; PIM/JIT.

data.Name: TP-04 | Phishing: Spearphishing Link
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Deliver a targeted credential-harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle, device-code or OAuth-related link to a privileged user. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: A successful phish against an administrator can bypass the need for technical exploitation and immediately grant access to high-impact control planes. Applicability: Core. Primary privileged assets at risk: Privileged Entra accounts, M365 administrators, Azure administrators, Support personnel. Attack-path stage: Acquire Privileged Identity. Detection opportunities: Defender for Office 365; SigninLogs; Identity Protection; URL click telemetry; Risk events after privileged-user link click. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Safe Links; Privileged Access Workstations; User training.

data.Name: TP-04 | Phishing: Spearphishing Voice
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Use voice social engineering to persuade privileged users or help-desk staff to disclose credentials, approve authentication, reset MFA or initiate a remote session. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Help desk and support workflows are attractive because they can alter authentication for high-value identities without requiring exploitation of the administrator endpoint. Applicability: Core. Primary privileged assets at risk: Help desk, Privileged users, Service desk processes. Attack-path stage: Acquire Privileged Identity. Detection opportunities: MFA reset audit; Help-desk records; Authentication-method changes after voice interaction. Defensive considerations: Strong identity-verification procedure; No privileged reset based on caller assertion; Phishing-resistant MFA.

data.Name: TP-04 | Brute Force: Password Spraying
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Attempt common or likely passwords across privileged or administrative identities while limiting attempts per account. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Even a single successful administrator login can provide substantial control. Privileged-account monitoring should therefore treat distributed or low-and-slow spraying as high risk. Applicability: Core. Primary privileged assets at risk: Entra administrators, VPN administrators, Domain administrators, Support accounts. Attack-path stage: Acquire Privileged Credentials. Detection opportunities: SigninLogs / authentication failures; Distributed-source spray detection; Targeting of privileged users. Defensive considerations: MFA; Smart lockout; Password protection; Disable legacy authentication.

data.Description: Reuse previously breached username/password pairs against administrative services and cloud identities. Detection opportunities: Leaked-credential detections; SigninLogs; Unfamiliar sign-in properties. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Unique credentials; Credential exposure monitoring.

data.Name: TP-04 | Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Generate repeated MFA requests to induce a privileged user to approve attacker-controlled authentication. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Push fatigue is especially dangerous for administrators because successful approval can immediately expose high-impact roles or eligible PIM assignments. Applicability: Core. Primary privileged assets at risk: Privileged Entra identities, PIM-eligible users, Support administrators. Attack-path stage: Bypass Privileged MFA. Detection opportunities: Repeated MFA prompts; Denied/expired MFA attempts; Authentication sequence anomalies. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Number matching; User education; Risk-based Conditional Access.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-04 | Generic System Integrator / MSP privileged-access profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Push fatigue is especially dangerous for administrators because successful approval can immediately expose high-impact roles or eligible PIM assignments. Applicability=Core; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-04 models targeting, acquisition, discovery, use, escalation and persistence of high-privilege identities and authentication material. It covers cloud administrators, customer administrative accounts, service accounts, application identities, PAM/PIM-eligible identities and—where applicable—Active Directory, local administrator, RMM and administrative-workstation credentials. TP-04 is intentionally identity/privilege-centric: detailed customer pivot belongs to TP-03, software supply-chain compromise to TP-05, and ransomware/destructive impact to TP-06. Conditional records must be filtered against the actual technology and customer-access model. This entry is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behavior has occurred.

data.Name: TP-04 | Steal Web Session Cookie
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Steal an authenticated browser-session cookie from a privileged user. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: A stolen administrator session can permit immediate access to Entra, Azure, M365 or customer administrative portals while avoiding a fresh password or MFA prompt. Applicability: Core. Primary privileged assets at risk: Admin browser sessions, Entra admin center, Azure portal, M365 portals, Customer portals. Attack-path stage: Steal Privileged Session. Detection opportunities: Session reuse from new IP/device; Impossible or atypical travel; Privileged action after session anomaly. Defensive considerations: Token/session protection; Managed admin devices; Privileged Access Workstations; Rapid session revocation.

data.Name: TP-04 | Steal Application Access Token
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Steal OAuth access tokens, refresh tokens, application tokens or managed-identity tokens that carry privileged permissions. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Privileged cloud operations can be performed programmatically. A stolen token may therefore provide administrator-level API capability even without knowledge of the user's password. Applicability: Core / Cloud. Primary privileged assets at risk: Microsoft Graph tokens, Azure ARM tokens, Service principals, Managed identities, Automation identities. Attack-path stage: Steal Privileged Token. Detection opportunities: Token use from unusual IP/client; API activity inconsistent with normal identity behavior; Unusual managed-identity token use. Defensive considerations: Least privilege; Token revocation; Protect workload credentials; Continuous Access Evaluation where available.

data.Name: TP-04 | Credentials from Password Stores: Windows Credential Manager
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Extract credentials from Windows Credential Manager or related Windows credential vaults. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Administrative workstations may contain cached or stored credentials for customer, RDP, network or management services. Those credentials can expand privilege beyond the initially compromised identity. Applicability: Windows Admin Endpoint. Primary privileged assets at risk: Windows Credential Manager, RDP credentials, Administrative workstation. Attack-path stage: Steal Privileged Credentials from Admin Endpoint. Detection opportunities: Vault access by unusual processes; Credential-dumping tool execution; EDR credential theft alerts. Defensive considerations: Credential Guard where applicable; PAW; No stored privileged credentials; EDR.

data.Name: TP-04 | Credentials from Password Stores: Password Managers
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Attempt to unlock, dump or abuse a privileged user's password-manager vault. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: System-integrator administrators may store many customer and infrastructure credentials in password managers. Compromise of one vault can create multi-system or multi-customer impact. Applicability: Core / Admin Endpoint. Primary privileged assets at risk: Enterprise password manager, Privileged credential vault, Customer support credentials. Attack-path stage: Steal Privileged Vault. Detection opportunities: Unusual vault export; New device/session accessing vault; Process access to local vault databases. Defensive considerations: Enterprise PAM; Hardware-backed MFA; Restrict exports; Separate privileged vaults; Monitor vault access.

data.Description: Enumerate or retrieve secrets from services such as Azure Key Vault or other cloud secret-management platforms. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: A privileged cloud identity may be authorised to access certificates, API keys, service credentials or application secrets. Detection opportunities: Secret-list/get operations by unusual identity; Bulk secret retrieval; Key Vault access after risky sign-in. Defensive considerations: RBAC least privilege; Managed identities; Private endpoints; PIM; Alert on bulk secret retrieval.

data.Description: Search scripts, configuration files, documentation and deployment artifacts for administrative passwords, tokens or connection strings. Defensive considerations: Secrets management; Secret scanning; Remove plaintext credentials; Least-privileged file access.

data.Name: TP-04 | Unsecured Credentials: Private Keys
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Acquire SSH keys, private certificates, PFX/PEM files or other key material used for privileged authentication. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Keys may authenticate administrators, automation or services without an interactive password. Stolen private keys can outlive password resets and bypass normal user-focused remediation. Applicability: Core / Infrastructure. Primary privileged assets at risk: SSH private keys, Client certificates, Service certificates, PFX/PEM files. Attack-path stage: Discover Privileged Keys. Detection opportunities: Unexpected private-key access/export; Reads of key stores by unusual processes; Certificate export audit. Defensive considerations: HSM/Key Vault; Non-exportable keys; Short-lived credentials; Rotation after compromise.

data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Access a cloud instance metadata endpoint to obtain managed-identity or instance credentials. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: If an attacker compromises a system used by an administrator or a managed workload, metadata credentials may expose a privileged workload identity with permissions distinct from the user account. Detection opportunities: Unexpected metadata endpoint access; Token use immediately after workload compromise; Unusual managed-identity API calls. Defensive considerations: Least privilege for managed identities; Harden metadata access; Network/workload isolation.

data.Name: TP-04 | OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Read LSASS memory on a Windows system where privileged users have authenticated to recover reusable credential material. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Administrative workstations, jump servers and management hosts are high-value credential concentration points. Credential dumping can expose domain, local or service administrator credentials and enable privilege expansion. Applicability: Windows / Hybrid Conditional. Primary privileged assets at risk: Admin workstation, Jump server, Domain credentials, Service credentials. Attack-path stage: Steal Privileged Windows Credentials. Detection opportunities: LSASS access telemetry; Credential-dumping alerts; Protected Process Light violations. Defensive considerations: Credential Guard; PAW; Prevent admins logging onto lower-trust systems; EDR.

data.Name: TP-04 | Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Request Kerberos service tickets for service accounts and crack them offline to recover account passwords. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Privileged or poorly governed service accounts can become an escalation path in customer or hybrid environments even when the system integrator's own tenant is cloud-only. Attack-path stage: Acquire Privileged Service Account. Detection opportunities: Abnormal TGS requests; High-volume service ticket requests; RC4 ticket patterns where applicable. Defensive considerations: gMSA; Long random passwords; Least privilege; AES-only where feasible.

data.Name: TP-04 | OS Credential Dumping: DCSync
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Abuse directory replication privileges to request password data from Active Directory as if acting as a domain controller. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: If a compromised privileged identity has replication rights, DCSync can expose highly privileged domain credentials and convert a limited customer foothold into domain-wide compromise. Applicability: Active Directory Customer / Hybrid. Primary privileged assets at risk: Domain controllers, KRBTGT, Domain administrators, Service accounts. Attack-path stage: Acquire Domain-Wide Credentials. Detection opportunities: Directory replication events from non-DC hosts; Replication rights assigned to unusual accounts; Defender for Identity detections. Defensive considerations: Restrict replication rights; Tiered administration; Monitor DCSync; Protect Domain Admin-equivalent privileges.

Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: An attacker who reaches a privileged Linux/customer account can preserve passwordless administrative access even if the original password is reset. Applicability: Linux / Infrastructure Conditional. Primary privileged assets at risk: Linux administrators, Cloud VMs, Appliances, Jump hosts. Attack-path stage: Persist Privileged SSH Access. Detection opportunities: authorized_keys modification; New SSH key after administrative session; Unexpected key fingerprint. Defensive considerations: Managed SSH certificates; File integrity monitoring; Restrict key changes.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-04 | Generic System Integrator / MSP privileged-access profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: An attacker who reaches a privileged Linux/customer account can preserve passwordless administrative access even if the original password is reset. Applicability=Linux / Infrastructure Conditional; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-04 models targeting, acquisition, discovery, use, escalation and persistence of high-privilege identities and authentication material. It covers cloud administrators, customer administrative accounts, service accounts, application identities, PAM/PIM-eligible identities and—where applicable—Active Directory, local administrator, RMM and administrative-workstation credentials. TP-04 is intentionally identity/privilege-centric: detailed customer pivot belongs to TP-03, software supply-chain compromise to TP-05, and ransomware/destructive impact to TP-06. Conditional records must be filtered against the actual technology and customer-access model. This entry is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behavior has occurred.

data.Description: Register an attacker-controlled device or authentication device against a compromised privileged identity. Defensive considerations: Restrict enrollment; Strong verification; Monitor admin device changes.

data.Name: TP-04 | Create Account: Cloud Account
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Create a new cloud identity and later assign it administrative roles or permissions. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: A new identity provides persistence independent of the initially compromised administrator and can be deliberately configured to appear like a service or support account. Applicability: Core / Cloud. Primary privileged assets at risk: Entra tenant, Cloud admin accounts, Service identities. Attack-path stage: Create Cloud Backdoor Administrator. Detection opportunities: New account followed by role assignment; Off-process provisioning; Privileged account created by unusual admin. Defensive considerations: Identity lifecycle governance; Approval; Alert on privileged account creation.

data.Name: TP-04 | Cloud Application Integration
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Create, consent to or abuse an OAuth/cloud application integration that holds high-value delegated or application permissions. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Application-based persistence can remain active independently of the administrator's interactive credentials and is especially dangerous when Graph or directory permissions are granted. Applicability: Core / Cloud. Primary privileged assets at risk: Enterprise applications, App registrations, Microsoft Graph, Service principals. Attack-path stage: Persist Through OAuth / Application. Detection opportunities: New app/service principal; Admin consent; High-risk Graph scopes; Unexpected application permissions. Defensive considerations: Admin consent workflow; Restrict user consent; App governance; Regular permission review.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-04 | Generic System Integrator / MSP privileged-access profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Application-based persistence can remain active independently of the administrator's interactive credentials and is especially dangerous when Graph or directory permissions are granted. Applicability=Core / Cloud; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-04 models targeting, acquisition, discovery, use, escalation and persistence of high-privilege identities and authentication material. It covers cloud administrators, customer administrative accounts, service accounts, application identities, PAM/PIM-eligible identities and—where applicable—Active Directory, local administrator, RMM and administrative-workstation credentials. TP-04 is intentionally identity/privilege-centric: detailed customer pivot belongs to TP-03, software supply-chain compromise to TP-05, and ransomware/destructive impact to TP-06. Conditional records must be filtered against the actual technology and customer-access model. This entry is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behavior has occurred.

Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Strong identity proofing; Alert on admin MFA changes.

data.Description: Modify Conditional Access policies, exclusions, trusted locations or authentication-strength requirements to facilitate attacker access. Defensive considerations: Restrict CA administration; PIM; Alert on policy changes; Protected emergency access accounts.

data.Name: TP-04 | Remote Services: Cloud Services
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-04 Privileged Access Compromise
data.Description: Use legitimate cloud services and management interfaces to reach resources accessible to the privileged identity. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Cloud administrative access can function as lateral movement across identity, M365, Azure and SaaS resources without malware or traditional network pivoting. Applicability: Core / Cloud. Primary privileged assets at risk: Azure, M365, Entra, SaaS admin services. Attack-path stage: Use Privileged Cloud Administration. Detection opportunities: Cross-service privileged activity; New service access by admin identity; Rapid resource traversal. Defensive considerations: Administrative segmentation; PIM; Conditional Access; PAW.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-04 | Generic System Integrator / MSP privileged-access profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Cloud administrative access can function as lateral movement across identity, M365, Azure and SaaS resources without malware or traditional network pivoting. Applicability=Core / Cloud; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. data.Description: Use legitimate RMM or remote desktop support software with compromised administrator credentials or operator sessions. data.Description: Disable or modify cloud logging, diagnostic settings, audit integrations or log export in order to hide privileged activity. Defensive considerations: Separate log administration; Protected external log storage; Alert on logging changes.

It covers cloud administrators, customer administrative accounts, service accounts, application identities, PAM/PIM-eligible identities and—where applicable—Active Directory, local administrator, RMM and administrative-workstation credentials. TP-04 is intentionally identity/privilege-centric: detailed customer pivot belongs to TP-03, software supply-chain compromise to TP-05, and ransomware/destructive impact to TP-06. Conditional records must be filtered against the actual technology and customer-access model. This entry is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behavior has occurred.
